ruling.question: What does '1 cup corn' mean in this catalogue?
ruling.answer: DRAINED KERNELS. One cup = 164 g drained solids (FDC 169214), one 15.25 oz can yields 298 g drained (FDC 169214 portion '1 can (303 x 406)'), and every corn gram in a spec is a drained gram.
ruling.why: It is the encoding the catalogue already uses for every other canned item a recipe drains (all 63 non-corn, non-pineapple 'N cans' lines are drained grams; densities.can is a drained yield with the literal note 'drained grams per 15oz can'; Chickpeas / Kidney / Cannellini macro rows are FDC 'canned, drained solids'); the engine already implements it (cost-recipes.ps1 DRAINED branch); densities.cup for corn is ALREADY the drained cup; and 17 of 34 corn lines were authored on it. The other 17 are internally consistent but on the wrong side of the catalogue's own convention.
ruling.single_encoding: densities.items.'Sweet Whole Kernel Corn'.can = 298 (cited), which is < 432 x 0.95 = 410.4 and therefore admits corn to $DRAINED with no engine change; the food-DB row moves to the FDC 169214 drained-solids basis per 100 g (the Chickpeas precedent); the 17 gross lines are re-expressed to drained grams (g x 298/432, rounded) so the drained engine reads them right; the 17 cup lines keep their grams.

items.subject: BOUNCE: the card cost widget and compute-v2 derive the package count from grams/gpu and never read pkg_g, so every drained-basis line on a live card buys one to nine packages fewer than the engine says the recipe needs
evidence: meal-prep\pipeline\tpl2-scaler-prefix.html:336 and :381 - `var required=(it.gpu>0)?it.grams*(nn/data.base)/it.gpu:0;` - the reader-facing package count is derived from GROSS grams-per-ounce, then :316 `var k=variable?0:(packageBasis>0?Math.max(1,Math.ceil(required/packageBasis-1e-9)):0)` divides it by the FEED's packageBasisUnits. :288 `function pkgs(it,nn){ return Math.max(1,Math.ceil(it.grams*(nn/data.base)/it.pkg_g - 0.02)); }` is the engine's rule and IS correct, and it has NO caller in the live template - grep finds callers only under meal-prep\archive\orig\built (the retired v1 card bodies).

meal-prep\pipeline\compute-v2-perserving.ps1:203 - `$req = if($gpu -gt 0){ [double][int]$ing.grams / $gpu } else { 0.0 }` with `$fallback = $pkgG/$gpu` - the same derivation, by design ('the card's required'), so cheapest_ps in v2-perserving.json shares the basis while everyday_ps (which reads the engine's k, line 195) does not. The two published numbers on one card now disagree about the same can.

items.root_cause: The buy-count rule exists in three places and only one of them was moved onto the drained basis. cost-recipes.ps1 buys ceil(grams / densities.can); the card widget and compute-v2-perserving both buy ceil((grams / gpu) / feed.packageBasisUnits), which is a GROSS-package unit count. While every canned item's densities.can equalled its net weight the two agreed and nothing could see the split; the moment an item is moved onto a real drained yield they diverge by exactly the drain factor. That is the [[two-copies-of-a-rule]] class, and package-cost-lib.ps1 already says outright that the JS is the authority and the PowerShell is its copy - so there are three copies and no test compares any two of them on a drained item.
